audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings claim Wither answers Pop Blossom: whys[4] "my Wither shuts the channel", wants.you[1] "Save Wither for the instant she channels R (Pop Blossom) so the stun never lands", and mid "Hold Wither for the exact moment she commits R — the massive movement and attack-speed slow ruins her combo".
audit.why: Wither is a movement-speed and attack-speed slow. It is not an interrupt and it does not cancel anything. Pop Blossom is also not flagged as a channel in the kit at all — compare Pantheon's Aegis Assault and Poppy's Keeper's Verdict, which both carry an explicit channel flag reading 'interruptible — any CC cancels it'. Neeko's R carries only dash and hardCC. So the ability is not interruptible in the first place, and even if it were, a slow would not do it. This is the most dangerous line in the matchup: it tells a Nasus to stand inside a 600-radius stun and press W, which loses the fight every time.
audit.corrected: Walk out of Pop Blossom's 600 radius during the preparation. Spend Wither after she lands, not on the cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early and spikes[0].text describe Blooming Burst as poison — "I just eat a little poison", "poison-pokes you off your Q last-hits".
audit.why: There is no poison anywhere in Neeko's kit. Blooming Burst is flat magic damage. Poison belongs to Cassiopeia, Teemo and Twitch, and the distinction matters because it changes nothing about how the chip is healed back — a Nasus reading 'poison' may think it ticks over time and mistime his Soul Eater sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says Blooming Burst "blossoms a second time if the first hit lands on a minion or champ".
audit.why: Riot's text is 'The seed blooms again on hitting champions or killing units'. Hitting a healthy minion does not re-bloom it — she has to kill the unit or hit a champion. That is the difference between standing next to a full-HP caster minion, which is safe, and standing next to an execute-range one, which is not.
audit.corrected: It blooms again on hitting a champion or killing a unit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The disguise is attributed to her W clone — mid says "the W clone juke: she'll disguise as a minion or my own teammate" and wants.foe[2] says "Disguise via W clone".
audit.why: Two different abilities are being merged. Inherent Glamour, her passive, is what makes her look like an ally champion or another unit. Shapesplitter (W) sends out a clone of Neeko herself and gives her bonus magic damage every third attack. The passive also has the tell that matters here: it breaks when she casts a damaging spell, when she takes immobilizing crowd control, or when the disguise takes damage equal to its healthbar. Wither is only a slow, so it will not break a disguise — another reason not to spend it on a suspicion.
audit.corrected: Name the passive as the disguise and give the break conditions.

edits.before: Neeko's whole early plan is her Q (Blooming Burst) — it blossoms a second time if the first hit lands on a minion or champ, so she farms and pokes you in one cast while I'm trying to soak Siphoning Strike stacks. I have no Wither until 3 and no ult, so I just eat a little poison and let Soul Eater lifesteal grind it back through last-hits. Don't walk up to trade autos into her Q range — there's nothing to win there, I'm only here to stack. At 3 I get Wither, which lets me peel a gank or punish her if she face-checks, but I still lose extended pokes.
edits.after: Neeko's whole early plan is her Q (Blooming Burst) — the seed blooms a second time when it hits a champion or kills a unit, so she farms and pokes you in one cast while I'm trying to soak Siphoning Strike stacks. It is flat magic damage, not poison, and Soul Eater lifesteal grinds it back through last-hits. I have no Wither until 3 and no ult, so don't walk up to trade autos into her Q range — there's nothing to win there, I'm only here to stack. At 3 Wither lets me peel a gank or punish a face-check, but I still lose extended pokes.

edits.before: Level 6 is the knife's edge: her R (Pop Blossom) is a channeled leap into an AoE stun-burst that chunks me hard, but it's slow and telegraphed. Hold Wither for the exact moment she commits R — the massive movement and attack-speed slow ruins her combo and she's squishy enough that my Fury of the Sands DPS plus an empowered Q flips it. Watch for the W clone juke: she'll disguise as a minion or my own teammate and try to land E (Tangle-Barbs) root from an angle I don't expect. If I respect the root and bait the ult, this stays even and tips my way on first item.
edits.after: Level 6 is the knife's edge: her R (Pop Blossom) leaps and knocks up, then stuns and burns on landing. Wither will not stop it — a slow is not an interrupt, so it neither cancels the leap nor spares me the stun. The only real answer is to walk out of its 600 radius during the preparation, which is hidden while she is disguised. Spend Wither once she has landed instead: her attack speed and movement die and Fury of the Sands plus an empowered Q flips it. The disguise is her passive, not W, and it breaks the moment she casts a damaging spell.

edits.after: Neeko's Q (Blooming Burst) double-pops on the wave and chips you off your Q last-hits before you have Wither to answer.

edits.after: Her R (Pop Blossom) is a delayed AoE stun-burst — walk out of its 600 radius rather than trusting Wither to stop it, then Fury of the Sands flips the all-in.

notes: The Wither-cancels-Pop-Blossom claim appeared in three places and is the kind of error a player acts on directly — it tells them to stand inside the stun radius. Note this matchup's content is written in first person ("I", "my") while the rest of the Nasus set is second person; I preserved the existing voice in each string rather than converting it, but the inconsistency is worth a pass. 283 games is the smallest sample in my slice, so the TRICKY / 7-10 label is not worth arguing with either way.
